sites.source: data_[block] &= ~(mask_ << shift);   (clear(), called by set(); the 32-bit word load of the read-modify-write; ptxas merges the &= and the following |= into one load and one store)

sites.source: data_[block] |= value << shift;   (set_from_zero(), called by set(); the word store of the read-modify-write, reached from common/unified/components/range_minimum_query_kernels.cpp:56 block_argmin.set(block_idx, argmin); and, for compute_lookup_large, from :84 and :109 superblocks.set_block_argmin)

thread_pair_example: compute_lookup_small, block 0 (size 1025 -> 129 blocks of 8 values -> 129 threads in one 512-thread block): thread 0 and thread 1 (block_idx 0 and 1, both in warp 0) update 4-bit entries of the same 32-bit word 0 of block_argmin (8 entries per word, aligned groups of 8 never straddle a warp): thread 1 loads the word (L160) before thread 0's store (L154) lands and then stores its merged value, overwriting thread 0's bits (lost update); also store/store on the same word. The same pattern holds for every word of block_argmin and, in compute_lookup_large, for the level-0 table and every superblock level (set_block_argmin uses the same bit_packed_span::set).
class_reason: The load and the store are plain global accesses (PTX ld.global.u32 / st.global.u32, SASS LDG.E / STG.E without .STRONG, no atomic, no fence, no barrier between threads of the launch). Several threads perform a non-atomic read-modify-write of one word: load vs store (RAW/WAR) and store vs store (WAW) on the same address, unordered -> data race of plain accesses (DR); no strong/atomic access, so no SC component. It is a true lost update, visible in the output.
buggy_expected: DR on the global word for block_argmin in compute_lookup_small and for the level-0 / per-level superblock words in compute_lookup_large: the pair (LDG at bit_packed_storage.hpp:160, STG at :154) of different lanes; reported file:line may be the inlined call sites range_minimum_query_kernels.cpp:56 / :84 / :109 depending on how the detector maps lines. The smoke run on sm_75 showed the symptom: 104 of 129 block_argmin entries and 742 superblock entries differ from the host brute force in the buggy build, 0 and 0 in the fixed build.

fixed.reason: The fix collates the work so one thread handles all entries that live in the same memory word (collation_width = 1 << (bits_per_word_log2 - ceil_log2(ceil_log2(small_block_size))) blocks per thread for compute_lookup_small; level0_collation_width = bits(word_type) and word_bits/round_up_pow2(level+1) per level for compute_lookup_large), so no two threads touch a word; each level is a separate launch. The same RMW instructions are still present in the fixed SASS (bit_packed_storage.hpp:160 LDG / :154 STG, now in a per-thread loop), so absence of a report relies on a detector reasoning about distinct words per thread, not on a code difference at the site.

The int64 instantiations (<long>) exist in the binary too but are not launched by the driver. No .STRONG token on any of these accesses. open_questions: The record's fix-commit file list names core/components/bit_packed_storage.hpp, but the two revisions differ only in common/unified/components/range_minimum_query_kernels.cpp (git diff 09d861f 64f1946 touches that one file); the packed-storage header is identical, so the racing sites are the same two lines at both revisions.

Warp mapping assumes the one-thread-per-block launch of generic_kernel_1d with default_block_size = 512 threads and 129 / (levels) work items: threads 0..7 share word 0 and are in warp 0; the word-sharing groups never straddle a warp for 4-bit entries but entries of other levels use 8/16-bit fields (more entries per word, still within a warp). A detector's thread-pair choice is not fixed by this oracle.
